question: Is key-side selectivity geometrically available at all? I.e. in the 128-dim per-head PRE-softmax query space (not DIAG-ROUTING's 512-dim post-softmax routing simplex), do MT eval queries carry energy outside the dominant subspace of the QA query second moment, and what MT/QA attention-mass ratio could an optimally placed key therefore reach?
variable_under_test: none (forward passes only, no training, no solve, no cache writes). Measured objects: Q0 = E_q[q q^T] per (layer, KV-head) on QA vs MT eval queries, on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge.
baseline_ref: DIAG-ROUTING (routing-simplex analogue: rho_MT=0.012, QA/MT cosine 0.99899, top-32 overlap 0.914) ; MECH-BETA (measured MT/QA mass_on_S ratio 1.043-1.051) ; LIT-020 (prediction rho_key in [0.15,0.6], ||dmu||/||qbar_MT|| >= 0.3, ratio >= 1.5)

numbers.note: diagnostic: no training/solve/eval-loss was run; two forward passes over the eval splits only

rho_qa_HELDOUT_control_at_r.definition: U_r from Q0 of QA documents with global-doc-index even; evaluated on Q0 of the DISJOINT odd QA documents. This is rho_key's own floor.

achievable_selectivity_bound_HELD_OUT.protocol: keys fitted on documents 0,1 (mod 4), reported on held-out documents 2,3; mass(q;k)=sigmoid(q.k/sqrt(d)-lse(q)) with lse over the 512 existing slots + visible causal prefix (frozen-context assumption); m keys -> logsumexp over keys
achievable_selectivity_bound_HELD_OUT.at_config: m=1 key, ||k||=4x median incumbent key norm, direction P_perp_32 qbar_MT (LIT-020)
achievable_selectivity_bound_HELD_OUT.free_form_optimiser_ratio_heldout: 0.885-1.12 (at mass_MT 0.003-0.16); FIT ratio 2.2-166 -> the in-sample optimum is entirely overfitting

mass_on_S.note: reproduces DIAG-ROUTING's 0.5697 / 0.58787 to 5-6 s.f. in an independent implementation, cross-validating the whole pipeline (no write was performed; this is the pre-write Phase-1 cartridge)

incumbent_per_slot_selectivity.caveat: in-sample max over 512 slots per head, no held-out control -> selection-biased, not comparable to the held-out bound above

wandb_note: https://wandb.ai/vqtri-purdue-university/SEACrowd/runs/kx4hsp5t is a SUPERSEDED first pass of the same script whose selectivity bound had no held-out split (its in-sample ratios up to 1e26 per head were pure overfitting); rho_key/eigen numbers are identical between the two runs to 6 s.f., which is an independent-process reproduction of item 1.
command: bash research_loop/results/DIAG-KEYSPACE/launch_diag_keyspace.sh  (PHASE1_CACHE=outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt, EVAL_SPECS=QA:data/qasper/eval/qasper_eval_QA.parquet,MT:data/qasper/eval/qasper_eval_MT.parquet, SLOTS_RUN_DIR=outputs/2026-07-28-19-27-08-continual_am_sparse/43a46f4b-..., N_SUB=8192, OPT_STEPS=300, WANDB_DISABLED=0, RUN_NAME=DIAG-KEYSPACE_query-geometry, WANDB_GROUP=B-ROUTE). No source file under cartridges/ was edited; imports pinned to /tmp/amsnap_kspace (git archive HEAD), verified from /tmp.
observations: rho_key sits at its own control floor. The fraction of MT query energy outside the top-r eigenspace of Q0^QA is 0.412/0.340/0.261/0.171/0.075 at r=4/8/16/32/64, but the held-out QA control (basis from one half of the QA documents, energy from the disjoint other half) is 0.403/0.328/0.251/0.166/0.074 at the same r -- MT exceeds QA's own out-of-subspace floor by 1.4-3.8%, and at the GPM 99%-energy rule MT is BELOW it (0.0113 vs 0.0118). No single head anywhere exceeds its control by more than 0.044 at r=32, and only layer 0 has a per-layer excess above 0.02. LIT-020 predicted rho_key in [0.15,0.6] against a near-zero floor; the raw 0.171 at r=32 falls inside that band only because the floor is 0.166. Item 3 is the same result stated as a distance: ||qbar_MT - qbar_QA||/||qbar_MT|| = 0.0700 (median 0.0666, max head 0.143) against a QA split-half control of 0.174 -- the mean-query gap between the two tasks is 2.5x SMALLER than the gap between two halves of QA itself, and 0 of 288 heads have it the other way round; mean-query cosine 0.99727 (QA control 0.98356). The prediction was >= 0.30; the routing-space shadow was 0.053, so query space bought a factor of 1.3, not the 5.7 needed. Item 2 confirms the key-blindness premise as a fact about the incumbent keys while refuting its consequence: the query second moment is genuinely high-dimensional (participation effective rank 5.09 QA / 5.30 MT, 106-107 of 128 dimensions to 99% energy) versus the routing Gram's 1.97, so the incumbent keys really do resolve far less than the queries contain -- but QA and MT occupy the SAME high-dimensional subspace (mean principal angle 4.3 deg at r=1, 10-14 deg for r=4..32; the two spectra and traces agree to ~0.3%). Item 4: with keys fitted on half the documents and scored on the held-out half, the best MT/QA attention-mass ratio any single key placement reaches at MT mass >= 0.08 is 1.2245 (LIT-020's P_perp_32 qbar_MT at 4x the median incumbent key norm, MT mass 0.109), while the identical pipeline run QA-document-group vs QA-document-group returns 1.0322 -- so the task-attributable selectivity is 1.19x, and at beta's bandwidth (mass >= 0.30) it falls to 1.080 against a 1.034 control. A free-form 300-step optimisation of the key direction reaches fit ratios of 2.2-166 and held-out ratios of 0.885-1.12: the in-sample optimum is overfitting, and the QA-vs-QA control reaches the same fit ratio (2.94 vs 2.82), which is what makes the negative credible. A random-direction key gives 1.011 and the difference-of-means direction gives 0.841 (worse than random, because dmu is dominated by sampling noise). Cross-validation: this independent implementation reproduces DIAG-ROUTING's cartridge mass to 5-6 s.f. (QA 0.56968 vs 0.5697, MT 0.58787 vs 0.58787) and the tf-idf-union MT/QA ratio 1.083. Caveats: Q0 is measured on the eval splits themselves (a deployed mechanism would build Q0^QA from reference data, which can only be worse); all masses use a frozen-context first-order model of adding one slot, ignoring the downstream residual-stream cascade B-CASCADE measured; the eval sets are 78 QA / 69 MT packed documents, and the QA-vs-QA control is what calibrates that sample size; keys are treated as post-RoPE vectors at the cartridge positions, so LIT-026's rotary hazards are outside this measurement; the free-form optimiser is a local search, so its held-out numbers are a lower bound on what a global optimum could reach, but the closed-form construction it fails to beat is the reported bound. Cost was 8.7 s of collection plus 0.8 s for 288+ EVDs (in line with SCOUT-KEYS' 86 s estimate); the 167 s bound optimisation is the addition SCOUT-KEYS did not budget, and it is what turned an uncontrolled in-sample ratio of 1e26 into a held-out 1.22.
